title: feat(squirrel-windows): inline installer logic; remove electron-winstaller dependency and its vendored binaries
body:
**Before:** Building the `squirrel` target pulled in the `electron-winstaller` npm package, whose `vendor/` directory ships prebuilt `Squirrel.exe`, `nuget.exe`, `SyncReleases.exe` and friends that dependency scanners keep flagging. To swap in your own Squirrel binaries you pointed `squirrelWindows.customSquirrelVendorDir` at a folder that was copied verbatim, bypassing every provisioning step. `squirrelWindows.remoteToken` set in config was silently ignored in favor of the environment.

**After:** `electron-builder-squirrel-windows` builds the installer itself with no `electron-winstaller` dependency. The Squirrel vendor toolset comes from the checksum-verified `squirrel.windows@1.1.1` electron-builder-binaries bundle (Squirrel.Windows 2.0.1 patched, with a real `nuget.exe` 6.14.0), `rcedit.exe` is provisioned from the `winCodeSign` toolset on every platform, and MSI builds merge in the shared WiX toolset. Version pinning and custom/local bundles go through the standard `toolsets.squirrel` setting, exactly like `toolsets.nsis` or `toolsets.winCodeSign`. `remoteToken` from config is honored, blank values fall back to `GH_TOKEN`/`GITHUB_TOKEN`, and MSI artifact names are derived correctly even when `.exe` appears inside the name.

This removes the vulnerable vendored binaries that electron-winstaller drags into every Squirrel build and gives Squirrel the same toolset provisioning story as the rest of electron-builder.

Resolves #9077

## What changed

**Squirrel.Windows implementation**
- New `packages/electron-builder-squirrel-windows/src/windowsInstaller.ts` replaces `createWindowsInstaller` from `electron-winstaller`. It copies `Squirrel.exe` into the app dir, renders the nuspec, runs `nuget pack`, runs `SyncReleases -u <remoteReleases> -r <releaseDir> [-t <token>]` when `remoteReleases` is set, releasifies with `Squirrel.exe --releasify` (`Squirrel-Mono.exe` under `mono` on macOS/Linux), passes `--loadingGif` / `--no-msi` as configured, and renames `Setup.exe` / `Setup.msi` to the configured artifact names. `RELEASES` and the `*-full.nupkg` / `*-delta.nupkg` artifacts are emitted as before.
- Lodash `template()` is gone: `template.nuspectemplate` now uses plain `<%- key %>` placeholders substituted via split/join, with the optional swiftshader / `vk_swiftshader_icd.json` entries pre-built as an `additionalFilesXml` fragment. All user-supplied metadata is passed through `escapeXml`.
- `install-spinner.gif` is bundled with the package and used as the default `loadingGif` when the project has none in `buildResources` (parity with electron-winstaller, which always supplied a spinner).
- A missing `Squirrel.exe` in the vendor dir and a missing `Setup.msi` when `msi: true` are now hard errors instead of silently producing a broken or incomplete installer.
- `rcedit.exe` is provisioned from the `winCodeSign` toolset on all hosts (host-arch: x64 for x64/arm64, x86 only for ia32) so `--releasify` can stamp version info and the icon into `Setup.exe` under Wine on non-Windows.
- `msi: true` merges the shared WiX 4.0.0.5512 toolset into the vendor dir and ships a `template.wxs` authored against the WiX v4 namespace.

**Toolset**
- New `toolset.ts` with `getSquirrelToolsetPath()` / `getWixToolsetPath()`. `toolsets.squirrel` accepts `"1.1.1" | ToolsetCustom | "latest"` (added to `ToolsetConfig`, `scheme.json` and the toolsets docs). `squirrel.windows@1.1.1` is the minimum and only known version; it ships a real `nuget.exe`, so there is no runtime `nuget.exe` download anywhere (earlier revisions of this PR fetched it at build time; that code and its `ELECTRON_BUILDER_SQUIRREL_*` env vars are removed).
- Every download is checksum-pinned (`squirrel.windows-2.0.1-patched.zip`, `wix-4.0.0.5512.2.7z`). A custom bundle (`ToolsetCustom`) must contain the `electron-winstaller/vendor/` subtree and goes through the same rcedit/WiX provisioning as the default one.
- `app-builder-lib/internal` now exports `getCustomToolsetPath`, `resolveToolsetVersion` and `getRceditBundle` for the target to reuse.

**Configuration / breaking**
- `squirrelWindows.customSquirrelVendorDir` is removed from `SquirrelWindowsOptions` and `scheme.json`; use `toolsets.squirrel` instead (see below).
- `electron-winstaller` is dropped from `electron-builder-squirrel-windows` dependencies, `test/package.json`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml` `allowBuilds` and the lockfile; the now-unused `@types/archiver` / `@types/fs-extra` dev dependencies go with it.
- electron-winstaller-only keys (`outputDirectory`, `appDirectory`, `exe`, `fixUpPaths`, `usePackageJson`, `extraFileSpecs`, `extraMetadataSpecs`, `skipUpdateIcon`, `setupExe`) are still rejected with `InvalidConfigurationError`, and that behavior is now covered by tests.

**Behavior fixes**
- An unknown pinned `toolsets.squirrel` version (only reachable through a programmatic config that bypasses the type and schema) throws `InvalidConfigurationError` listing the known versions instead of reaching the downloader with `checksums: undefined`, which would have disabled integrity verification.
- `squirrelWindows.remoteToken` is forwarded from config (previously dropped). A blank or whitespace-only value is treated as unset and falls back to `GH_TOKEN` then `GITHUB_TOKEN`; the chosen token is trimmed.
- `setupMsi` is derived by replacing only the trailing `.exe` (`/\.exe$/i`), so `my.exe.app-Setup.exe` yields `my.exe.app-Setup.msi` rather than `my.msi.app-Setup.exe`.

**Docs**
- `toolsets.md`: `squirrel` row and platform note (native on Windows; `mono` plus Wine-hosted `rcedit` elsewhere).
- `squirrel-windows.md`: Linux `mono` install hint and where the vendor binaries come from.
- `migration/v27-breaking-changes.md` + `v26-to-v27.md`: `customSquirrelVendorDir` removal, why it is not a 1-to-1 rename, and the `toolsets.squirrel` replacement.
- `tutorials/offline-air-gapped-builds.md`: cache path for `squirrel.windows@1.1.1` and the bundles a Squirrel build needs offline.

**Tests**
- `squirrelWindowsOptionsTest.ts` (new, 55 tests): `computeEffectiveDistOptions` mapping for `useAppIdAsId`, `name`, `loadingGif`, `remoteReleases`, `remoteToken` (config vs env, blank, trimming), `iconUrl` fallbacks, `msi` validation, legacy-key rejection, `artifactName` / `setupMsi` derivation and nuspec `projectUrl` injection.
- `squirrelWindowsInstallerTest.ts` (new, 45 tests): `convertVersion`, `escapeXml`, `renderNuspecTemplate`, `buildAdditionalFilesXml`, and `createWindowsInstaller` with `exec` mocked to assert the exact `nuget` / `SyncReleases` / `Squirrel` argument lists, MSI handling, rename behavior and rendered nuspec content on every OS.
- `squirrelWindowsToolsetTest.ts` (new, 8 tests): `ToolsetCustom` resolution, pinned `1.1.1` download with checksum, unknown-version rejection before any download, error propagation.
- `squirrelWindowsTargetTest.ts` (new): `select7zipArch` copy/skip behavior. `squirrelWindowsSecurityTest.ts`: null-byte path cases.
- Windows integration (`squirrelWindowsTestSuite.ts`, run across the generated `wcs-*` winCodeSign matrix): new `x64 no msi`, `useAppIdAsId and explicit loadingGif` and `iconUrl not specified` cases; snapshots regenerated.
- `packTester.ts`: the nuspec check inside `checkSquirrelResult` was dead code (it only ran when `checkOptions == null`, which never happened). It now always runs, asserts the config-derived metadata fields against the `.nuspec` that `nuget.exe` actually packed, and tolerates nuget's `System.Uri` trailing-slash canonicalization of `projectUrl`. `convertVersion` is imported from our module instead of `electron-winstaller`.

## Breaking changes

The changeset marks **`electron-builder-squirrel-windows`** and **`app-builder-lib`** as **major** (they are in the same linked release group).

`squirrelWindows.customSquirrelVendorDir` is removed. It pointed at a directory whose contents were the vendor files and was copied verbatim; `toolsets.squirrel` instead takes a version pin or a `ToolsetCustom` whose `url` points at a bundle containing an `electron-winstaller/vendor/` subtree, and that bundle still gets `rcedit.exe` (and WiX for `msi: true`) provisioned on top.

```json5
// Before (removed)
{ "squirrelWindows": { "customSquirrelVendorDir": "./my-vendor" } }

// After: pin a version…
{ "toolsets": { "squirrel": "1.1.1" } }
// …or supply your own bundle whose electron-winstaller/vendor/ holds the binaries.
// A bare file:// directory is used as-is; a remote/archive url needs a checksum.
{ "toolsets": { "squirrel": { "url": "file:///abs/path/to/squirrel-toolset" } } }
```

## How

The installer logic is a trimmed port of `electron/windows-installer`'s `src/index.ts` restricted to what electron-builder actually uses (`usePackageJson: false`, signing handled by `packager.signIf`), driving the vendor executables through `builder-util`'s `exec` (directly on Windows, via `mono` elsewhere). `prepareSignedVendorDirectory` collapses to a single path: resolve the `squirrel.windows` toolset (pinned, `latest`, or `ToolsetCustom`) via the shared `downloadBuilderToolset` / `getCustomToolsetPath` helpers, layer `rcedit.exe` from the `winCodeSign` toolset and, for MSI, the WiX toolset plus `template.wxs` on top, then sign `Squirrel.exe`. `toolsets.squirrel` reuses the existing `ToolsetConfig` plumbing so pinning, custom bundles, caching and the offline story behave like every other toolset.

## Testing

CI on `1987c94`: 60 of 62 checks finished green (the one non-success is `run-docker-build`, skipped by design) with `merge-smart-cache` and `faraday/cage` still running at the time of writing; the previous head `e18b4df` was fully green. Locally, `TEST_FILES=squirrelWindowsOptionsTest,squirrelWindowsInstallerTest,squirrelWindowsToolsetTest pnpm ci:test` passes 108/108 tests (55 + 45 + 8). The Windows integration suite (including the new `no msi`, `useAppIdAsId`/`loadingGif` and `iconUrl` cases and the regenerated `wcs-*` snapshots) runs in CI on the Windows shards.
